_comment: Pairs of taught words whose example translations are the same sentence in a
language, where the English pack distinguishes them.
`vocabulary:translation:qa` reports every such pair and fails on one that is
not listed here. The point is not that sharing a sentence is wrong — the
English pack shares 27 of its own — but that it should be a decision. When
이메일 and 문자 shared one Japanese sentence, an email and a text message were
being taught as the same thing, and nothing said so for several releases.
Each entry names the languages that merge the pair and why the merge is
acceptable. The reason is always the same shape: the target language has one
ordinary word where English has two, and inventing a distinction it does not
make would read worse than sharing a sentence.
Which merges are legitimate is ultimately a question for a speaker of the
language, and no speaker has read any of these — see I-17. This file records

강하다·거세다.why: strong and fierce, of wind; Portuguese reaches for forte for both

고약하다·불쾌하다.why: nasty and unpleasant, of a smell; Portuguese has one ordinary word

공원·산책하다.why: walking in the park and taking a walk in the park; only English separates the noun from the activity here

구역·지역.why: zone and area; one word in Spanish and Vietnamese

기다리다·잠깐.why: wait a moment and wait just a moment; the intensifier has no idiomatic counterpart

기다리다·잠깐만.why: the same pair with the other 잠깐만 sentence

끝내다·숙제.why: I finished the homework and I finished my homework; the English barely separates them either

낮추다·줄이다.why: lower and turn down, of a volume; one verb in these languages

내내·종일.why: all day and the whole day

대단히·정말.why: thank you very much indeed and thank you very much

되찾다·회복하다.why: got back and recovered, of health

들리다·분명히.why: I can hear it clearly and I heard it clearly; the modality is not carried

막다·차단하다.why: blocked and blocked off, of a road

말다·염려.why: don't worry and don't be concerned

멈추다·정지.why: stopped and came to a stop, of a car

수고하다·애쓰다.why: thank you for your hard work and thank you for going to such trouble

쉬다·잠시.why: rest a little and rest for a moment

아무·언제든지.why: come any time and please come any time; the politeness is in the ending, not in the adverb

없애다·제거하다.why: got rid of and removed, of a stain

오래·오랫동안.why: a long time and for a long time

요청하다·청하다.why: requested and asked for, of help

정리하다·치우다.why: tidied and cleared, of a desk
